howto.name: PrivaTools re-encodes via FFmpeg
howto.text: One more lossy generation, in exchange for a format that plays essentially everywhere.

howto.name: Convert and download
howto.text: Click Convert. MP3 plays essentially everywhere, which Ogg still does not, at the cost of one more lossy generation.

faq.a: OGG Vorbis isn't supported by some players, car stereos, and editing apps; MP3 is nearly universal. Both are lossy, so this is about compatibility, not quality.
Re-encoding one lossy format to another (transcoding) loses a little quality. Choose 256–320 kbps to keep it minimal.
The file is converted by FFmpeg on the PrivaTools server, not a third-party service, and the temporary input and output are removed by response cleanup after the result is sent.
